operational_conclusion: Refuse any broad or casual deletion of /opt/nq-trial. Because the writer is already stopped, the safe reset is to quarantine the complete SQLite set and copy the configurations, checksum and package that quarantine, verify it, and preserve the archive outside the service account's write boundary before replacing or removing anything. Starting afterward creates a new evidence history; it is not recovery of the old condition and does not prove that the old condition was resolved.
components_required: For the documented legacy-operational runtime, nq-monitor and the nq-witness compatibility publisher are the required pair.
/opt/nq-trial/state/nq.db, nq.db-wal, and nq.db-shm must be preserved together as the stopped-writer evidence set because all three are present.
/opt/nq-trial/etc/publisher.json and /opt/nq-trial/etc/aggregator.json must be preserved to reconstruct what was observed.
The installed binary versions and SHA-256 digests must be recorded before binary removal.
components_optional: nq-suite, nq-witness-tool, and application-specific check packs are optional to the legacy-operational profile and are not listed in this trial.
/opt/nq-trial/state/liveness.json is not required to reconstruct the durable evidence history.
/opt/nq-trial/build-cache is not required after it has been checked for misplaced records.
first_meaningful_result: The first meaningful reset result is a verified archive preserved outside the service account's write boundary. After the fresh runtime starts, its first meaningful operational result is a host row; process startup, an empty overview, or creation of a new nq.db is not sufficient.

recovery_or_next_action: Keep the monitor writer stopped throughout capture. The scenario states that it is already stopped.

Before removing binaries, run `/opt/nq-trial/bin/nq-monitor --version`, `/opt/nq-trial/bin/nq-witness --version`, and `sha256sum /opt/nq-trial/bin/nq-monitor /opt/nq-trial/bin/nq-witness`, and retain their output in the operator's installation/audit record. The documentation does not specify that record's path, so I will not invent one.

Run the documented archive-first block with the literal prefix: `(
  set -eu
  NQ_PREFIX='/opt/nq-trial'
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  quarantine="$NQ_PREFIX/archive-before-reset-$stamp"
  install -d -m 0700 "$quarantine"

  for file in \
    "$NQ_PREFIX/state/nq.db" \
    "$NQ_PREFIX/state/nq.db-wal" \
    "$NQ_PREFIX/state/nq.db-shm"; do
    if test -e "$file"; then
      mv "$file" "$quarantine/"
    fi
  done
  cp -p "$NQ_PREFIX"/etc/*.json "$quarantine/"
  sha256sum "$quarantine"/* > "$quarantine/SHA256SUMS"
  tar -C "$NQ_PREFIX" -czf "$NQ_PREFIX/archive-before-reset-$stamp.tar.gz" \
    "archive-before-reset-$stamp"
  sha256sum "$NQ_PREFIX/archive-before-reset-$stamp.tar.gz"
)`.

Verify the quarantined members and archive, retain the printed archive digest, and preserve the archive outside the service account's write boundary. The documentation supplies neither that external destination nor the site's verification/retention procedure, so the destructive phase must pause until the operator supplies them.
Do not discard the in-prefix quarantine until the independently preserved copy and its digest have been verified under the applicable retention policy.

Only after verification may liveness.json be recreated, configurations be replaced for the fresh trial, and binaries be removed or replaced. Binary removal follows the version/digest record; it does not remove durable evidence.
Treat build-cache as deletable only after checking it contains no operator-authored configuration, evidence, backup, decision artifact, or witness artifact.
Do not combine reset with removal of the service account or backups; either requires a separate administrative and retention decision.
Starting the monitor after the database set has been quarantined intentionally creates a new history. Keep the old archive available for audit and reconstruction.
